text:
maria.s: heads up — on the POC with FinSolve, their app can't complete the TLS handshake when hitting our private endpoint via Azure Private Link. They see cert errors and some OCSP failures. timeline is tight, they want Dedicated by EOW :grimacing:

devon.k: can you paste the client-side error and a quick dig output? also which subscription/region — azure peering quirks depend on vnet/private-dns

maria.s: here's what they sent: 
```
curl -v https://api.internal.redwood.svc --resolve api.internal.redwood.svc:443:10.1.5.12
* Connected to api.internal.redwood.svc (10.1.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Unknown CA
* SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain
```

Plus they have this openssl output: 
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.1.5.12:443 -servername api.internal.redwood.svc -status
OCSP response: no response sent
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
```

alex.t: couple quick thoughts — 1) If the client is connecting to the IP directly, SNI still needs to match the cert CN/SAN (they used -servername, so that's ok). 2) OCSP stapling missing could be because our edge can't reach OCSP responder from that VNet (Azure NAT / outbound rules). 3) Could be split-horizon DNS pointing to an internal proxy that terminates TLS with a different cert.

sean.p: +1. Can we get them to run `dig +short api.internal.redwood.svc` and `curl -v --resolve api.internal.redwood.svc:443:10.1.5.12 https://api.internal.redwood.svc/health` and paste outputs? Also ask for packet capture if possible.

maria.s: they ran dig: `10.1.5.12` (IPv4). They said their corporate firewall uses forced egress through a proxy that only allows TLS via an outbound inspection proxy (mTLS break). They also said our cert chain validation works for public endpoints but fails on private because our intermediate isn't served.

devon.k: OK — two immediate checks: 
1) On the VNet side, ensure outbound to our CA's OCSP endpoints is allowed (tcp/80 or 443 depending on responder). We publish OCSP endpoints in config but common ones are `ocsp.example-ca.com:80`.
2) Confirm the endpoint's TLS stack is serving full chain (leaf + intermediate). Quick test from our side: 
```
openssl s_client -connect api.internal.redwood.svc:443 -servername api.internal.redwood.svc -showcerts
```
If intermediate missing, the client (esp proxies) will reject.

alex.t: also watch for Azure Private Link when using service endpoint mapping — if user's DNS forwards to their on-prem DNS via conditional forwarders, they might be resolving an internal proxy IP instead of the PL IP. Ask if they see any proxy headers in responses.

maria.s: they captured a small proxy log: `CONNECT api.internal.redwood.svc:443 HTTP/1.1 502 tls_handshake_failure` and `client-ip: 172.17.4.9`

sean.p: looks like their outbound inspection proxy is doing MITM, dropping our chain. Two options: (A) ask their security team to whitelist the DC egress so proxy allows passthrough for our destination, or (B) switch POC to use a Private Endpoint with enforced TLS passthrough (no intercept) — requires their firewall rules change.

maria.s: they're pushing back on firewall changes — security team won't allow passthrough without cert pinning / managed trust. Any quick workaround for the POC so we can demo features?

devon.k: for a short-term workaround: 1) we can provide a customer-specific cert chain signed by their internal CA (if they trust it) so the proxy will forward. 2) or offer to run a dedicated gateway in their VNet (Redwood Private gateway) — that's more setup but avoids proxy interception. Both have ops/infra implications; I'll DM infra-bot to prep an estimate.

infra-bot: Created ticket #INF-4123 for "POC: Private gateway + Dedicated cert option — FinSolve". Assigned to eng-infra, ETA for estimate: 2 business days. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123

maria.s: perfect. I'll relay both options and see if they can unblock with their security. Also flagged pricing impact if we need a dedicated gateway for the POC (could push to Dedicated SKU).

alex.t: one more diagnostic if they can run it: `openssl s_client -connect 10.1.5.12:443 -servername api.internal.redwood.svc -showcerts -status` and paste full cert chain — that'll confirm missing intermediate vs OCSP panics.

maria.s: got it. i'll collect that and follow up. thanks all :pray: 

sean.p: fyi, if they do accept dedicated gateway we should pre-configure our docs for azure peering/NAT egress rules and list the OCSP endpoints to whitelist — saves back-and-forth. I'll draft a short checklist after INF-4123 is created.
